skos:Concept.skos:scopeNote: {"id": "b7cdd640-6a27-4241-85e2-db6035bc4272", "value": "A chronological series of components or phases within the geographical limits of a locality. The sequence may or may not related to an overarching archaeological period."}
{"id": "bd2f8cbf-00fa-4f96-8630-05b56c921a36", "value": "Stoneware, is a hard, dense, high-fired, non-porous ceramic. It can be coarse or find-textured and is commonly stone-coloured."}

{"id": "e32382e3-0ce6-492a-b16e-c0503548e1ef", "value": "Earthenware is a relatively soft, low-fired, porous, ceramic.Either coarse-textured or find-grained, earth-coloured. OR A general term referring to all wares made from fired clay, including earthenware, stoneware, porcelaneous ware and porcelain - or an object made from such substances. (see https://gotheborg.com/glossary/ceramics.shtml)"}

{"id": "e36a679a-fb17-4dc3-abd4-ea515b330b0c", "value": "Any subgroup of elements within an industry or main culture tradition, such as a ceramic tradition, that is distinguished from the whole on the basis of some aspect of appearance or composition."}

{"id": "b037fad8-2aaf-48ef-8ba0-fe38a4b5fa1d", "value": "Tradition is a term describing the persistence in a given area over a period of time in individual attributes, artifact types, in this case ceramics, or technologies; a culture that exists for an extended period of time and usually over an extended area."}

{"id": "ec3ac81a-66e4-43b4-9cfb-285801ce07a7", "value": "Porcelain is a hard, dense, high to very high-fired, non-porous ceramic. White to grey-white in colour, fine textured body, and translucent in thin-section."}

{"id": "a598851a-b831-4ba3-ba1f-340fb8665286", "value": "This period is the era of the last great Islamic Empires. The Ottoman Empire which had started as a small Turkic state in Anatolia in the early fourteenth century emerged in the second half of the fifteenth century as a major military and political force. The Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453 and the Mamluk Empire in 1517. They dominated much of Anatolia the Balkans the Near East and North Africa until the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire after World War I. The Safavids who established Shia Islam as the dominant faith of Iran ruled from 1501\u20131722 and were the greatest dynasty to emerge from Iran. The other great dynasty that oversaw a remarkable artistic and architectural output was the Mughals. Founded by Babur the Mughals (c. 1526\u20131858) ruled over the largest Islamic state in the Indian subcontinent. | Parts of Northern Sudan were occupied by the Ottoman Empire from the 1560s mainly forts along the Nile | The area of the Red Sea coast particularly around the long-lasting coastal trading towns of Suakin and Masawwa was conquered over the 16th century CE by the Ottomans and administered from across the Red sea as part of the Eyalet of Habes/Habesh beginning in the mid 16th century. 1517CE - 1880CE"}

{"id": "de49469d-5556-4033-84ed-534a80e23492", "value": "Longlasting and distinct ceramic tradition found in Eastern Sudan (near the borders with Ethiopia and Eritrea) with a number of sub-traditions. Its primary characteristic is the use of scraping for both thinning and decoration which is present in almost all sub-traditions (excluding very earliest sites). 5000BCE - 400CE. | Longest and most complex phase of the wider Atbai Ceramic Tradition. In addition to its distinct ceramics can be characterised by large village sites and polished stone tools. | Ceramic tradition characterised by scraped ware and red-topped ware with an incised herringbone pattern. Also associated with a large residential village-based sedentary or semi-sedentary settlement pattern and some evidence for prestige goods via porphyry maceheads."}

{"id": "408dcd5f-2183-4131-a36e-e69dd1ec1f51", "value": "The sites of the Gash Group are recorded along the Gash Delta Kassala Province and in the alluvial plains south of it. The main site is Mahal Teglinos (K1). The material culture is dominated by scraped vessels the rest of the ceramics are mostly decorated with rim band designs: simple dash rouletted punctuate zoned and horizontal zig-zag patterns. The flaked stone industry is basically microlithic with a small amount of blades. (Fattovich 1993) | In the Early Phase of the Gash Culture there are some transitional phenomena. Most artefacts were found in the excavations at Shurab el Gash which may be regarded as a transitional Butana/Gash site. The earliest funerary stelae most likely go back to this period. More finds are from Mahal Teglinos and ES 1. The ceramics include bowls decorated with comb impressed bands which often extend to the body of the vessel and/or rim bands made by impression. There are also plain bowls with notches on top of the lip accurately scraped and wiped ware and a vegetal tempered ware. The lithic industry shows a significant percentage of ninety-degree core flakes single platform flakes and geometrics are the most characteristic tools. The subsistence economy includes the keeping of cattle and sheep/goats but hunting and gathering is an important component. With the appearance of elements from Early Kerma and C-Group there is a beginning of trade visible."}

{"id": "25c30c22-87e0-4499-a9ec-6d8478c36f9e", "value": "{\"id\": \"d9789332-3f2d-46c6-8c0a-7aebe0a4123d\", \"value\": \"c. AD 650\u20131500. \"Triggered by increased demand for West African resources early Islamic trans-Saharan commerce became profoundly important: it established the first true connection between West Africa and the wider \u2018world system\u2019 a vital precursor to European involvement in West Africa; it brought significant economic inputs to Central Islamic lands most crucially gold and slaves; and not least it introduced Islam itself to West Africa (Insoll 2003; Mitchell 2005). \"\"}"}

{"id": "cfcb47a6-6106-4497-84a3-dd703a962dd0", "value": "The Aksumite Culture has a ceramic tradition which is widespread in central Tigray. It begins with an early phase which dates before the political unit which we know from written sources. The ceramic tradition of central Tigray (c. 1000 BC\u2013AD 700) is represented by several sites around Yeha and Aksum (Michels 2005; Sernicola 2008). This region has been more extensively investigated and a reasonably solid cultural sequence has been outlined from the combined results of the stratigraphic sequence of the ceramics radiocarbon dating of almost fifty charcoal samples cross-dating on fragments of foreign vases and glass artefacts and coins. | Classic Aksumite phase ceramic assemblages are characterized by round basins with a ledge rim and foot-rings globular jars with high neck small bowls with foot-rings and a ledge rim often decorated with vertical corrugations alternating with bands of incised diamonds."}

{"id": "2bdd2136-aa98-4d45-b83f-9357aca4a057", "value": "{\"id\": \"541d22db-54d4-466b-a423-4f1f9a0c7420\", \"value\": \"Description: \"Kobadi Tradition pottery as it occurs in the southern Gourma is almost identical to that of the M\u00e9ma (MacDonald 1994) with the exception of two variant ware types. The more \"typical\" Kobadi Tradition wares are globular simple rimmed vessels with bands of complex punctate stabbed comb (Comb) or pivoted spatula (P. spatula) decor underlain by either twosted or braided twine roulettes (Twist Tw and Braid Rw) (Table 1 fig. 3a-c). The first of the two variant wares consists of open simple rimmed bowls with a distinctive undecorated band beneath the lip underlain by braided or twisted twine roulettes and sometimes impressed cord-wrapped stick (ICS) (fig. 3). The second variant ware is comprised of large vessels (40-60 cm internal diameter) featuring slightly out-turned rims and invariable \"wavy\" stabbed comb decor (fig. 3.e.). The majority of the assemblage recovered from excavations at Wind\u00e9 Koroji Sud-Ouest were sponge spicule tempered (60.7 % of rims) as is typical of the Kobadi Tradition although sand and grog temper were also present (Table 1). Interestingly the latter temper types only occurred in the two variant wares which both showed great variation in fabric with examples of them known in all three temper types.\" | 1200BCE-1000BCE\"}"}

{"id": "b199c6e6-55b9-4e2d-9ecc-867eec0934a5", "value": "{\"id\": \"7b59e922-ff46-4fa0-839f-271ec4456149\", \"value\": \"Description: \"The ceramics of the Wind\u00e9 Koroji tradition are characterized by numerous shallow cauldrons and tighly closed jars both featuring everted rims (fig. 4a-c). Alo distinctive but much less common are broad basins (fig. 4d). Open bowls and globular simple rimmed vessels are also present (fig. 4e-f). The most common decors are twisted twine roulettes (Twisted Tw) impressed or roulette cord-wrapped stick (ICS/CSR) and impressed netting (Net/Fabric) (Table 1). The latter motif is especially striking occurring both tightly applied to the vessel and loosely impressed. Highly distinctive but less common decor types include knotted twine roulettes (often featuring multiple knots) (fig. 4c) braided twine roulette (which produce a \"herringbone effect\") and a curious type of \"applied\" plastic decor. This latter motif features the semi-perforation of the pot with a blunt tipped object and a subsequent re-finishing of resultant voids and bulbs (fig. 4d). \" The site of Wind\u00e9 Koroji Ouest (WKO) the type site of the facies is located at the centre of the Wind\u00e9 Koroji complex in the vicinity of a seasonal Songhai hamlet. | Description: \"Le faci\u00e8s de Wind\u00e9 Koroji bien qu'apparent\u00e9 aux faci\u00e8s n\u00e9olithiques de la vall\u00e9e du Tilemsi offre plusieurs particularit\u00e9s. Il se caract\u00e9rise au niveau de la c\u00e9ramique par des formes en \"chaudrons\" peu profonds et des jarres \u00e0 ouverture r\u00e9duite. La plupart des bords sont assez \u00e9vers\u00e9s. Les poteries sont en r\u00e8gle g\u00e9n\u00e9rale d\u00e9graiss\u00e9es \u00e0 la chamotte et d\u00e9cor\u00e9es au peigne filet\u00e9 souple \u00e0 la cordelette roul\u00e9e ou bien encore par impression de nattes ou de filets. L'industrie lithique est tr\u00e8s particuli\u00e8re. Les armatiures de fl\u00e8ches salicyforme ou foliac\u00e9es en silex pr\u00e9dominent au c\u00f4t\u00e9 d'une industrie grossi\u00e8re sur gr\u00e8s. Les haches polies de tailles variable sont aussi pr\u00e9sentes. Les sondages sir me soye de Wind\u00e9 Koroji ont r\u00e9v\u00e9l\u00e9 deux structures pratiquement affleurante : le fond d'une hutte circulaire et une petite fosse remple de mat\u00e9riel. Les restes de faune comprennent des bovins des ovicaprins un grand nombre de mammif\u00e8res sauvages et des poissons adapt\u00e9s aux eaux peu profondes. Les meules sont abondantes. Les restes de pal\u00e9oflore ont livr\u00e9 des esp\u00e8ces sauvages et quelques graines de Pennisetim sp. vraisemblablement domestique. Une \u00e9conomie pastorale semble pouvoir \u00eatre rattach\u00e9e au faci\u00e8s Wind\u00e9 Koroji. \"\"}"}

{"id": "2d4404c0-c57f-4aed-9693-da13e4a615b0", "value": "Contentious chronological term referring to a type of pottery characterised by the use of several different wavy line decorations with additional dot marks between them found both in the Nile Valley and across the wider Sahel-Sahara belt. Assumed to be a successor to the Wavy Line by early researchers (e.g. Arkell) associated with the Khartoum Neolithic vs Khartoum Mesolithic but proven to be found in Khartoum Mesolithic/Neolithic occupations from beginning to end and found earlier than the Wavy Line in Sahara-Sahel contexts. Chronological associations have yet to be fully deciphered but current estimates suggest 10000BP - 4000BCE."}

{"id": "e8716038-1675-4f53-b3c2-167b71350500", "value": "Archaeology increasingly attests the complex and cosmopolitan nature of societies in medieval Ethiopia (c. seventh to early eighteenth centuries AD). Four religious traditions are relevant to this theme: Islam Judaism. Christianity and Indigenous religions. Ethiopia's medieval archaeology is much less well known than the prehistory of the country. | Characterised by its Gondarene architecture and castles."}

{"id": "ed98ce3c-177b-4824-9899-238bb3e86c5e", "value": "{\"id\": \"88871e6d-e8c7-43a5-ada7-318534ca63cc\", \"value\": \"Description: \"despite the antiquity of this trade only in the last few centuries BC did it link the area of study [from Middle East to East Asia reaching as far apart as West Africa and the American Pacific coast]\". | Description: 7th - 8th Century AD. Based on chemical analysis Chibuene series beads probably came from the Middle East east of the Euphrates with the Sasanian Persian Gulf trade. Possibly found at Nqoma western Botswana and potentially at sites in East Africa. Around the middle-to-late 10th century importation of Zhizo beads ceased and Chibuene\u2019s role as a port serving Indian Ocean trade and the interior of southern Africa ended. These beads are also found at several sites in West Africa beginning in around the 8th century AD but seem to vanish from trade there by the end of the first millennium AD.\"}"}

{"id": "a5349d90-a1af-4e6c-b835-1da69c01841e", "value": "The Neogene includes the Miocene and Pliocene epochs (23700000\u20131600000 years ago) and is considered by some to encompass the time up to the present. The Neogene which means newborn was designated as such to emphasize that the marine and terrestrial fossils found in the strata of this time were more closely related to each other than to those of the preceding period called the Paleogen. | On the geologic time scale the youngest epoch of the Tertiary or of the more recently designated Neogene following Miocene and preceding the Pleistocene epoch of the Quaternary period. It extends from about 5.3 million to 2.58 million years ago."}

{"id": "15430ea0-5ecc-4274-be74-3fe095b7c221", "value": "The African Stone Age spans the first 2.5 Ma of human prehistory beginning with the world\u2019s earliest stone tool production and continuing through the historical period of European colonization. The African Stone Age includes a tremendous diversity in terms of the characteristics of its industries and the life ways engaged in by its makers. Archaeological research on African stone tool industries has had wide-ranging impacts on our understanding of processes of human evolution and the organization of past human societies. The Stone Age conventionally encompasses three broad phases: Early Stone Age (ESA) Middle Stone Age (MSA) and Later Stone Age (LSA). Use more specific type where known. | This is the first and earliest period of the Stone Age occuring during the Plio-Pleistocene and dating from 2.1 mya to 0.2 mya for southern Africa. The Early Stone Age is characterised by the oldest known cultural material produced by hominins and is generally characterised by simple stone tool industries including the Oldowan dating between 2.1 mya and 1.7 mya and the Acheulean dating between 1.4 mya and 0.2 mya . In Southern Africa the earliest stone tools include simple flakes struck from cobbles core and pebble tools and in later stages include intentionally shaped handaxes cleavers and picks; final or transitional stages have tools that are smaller than the preceding stages and include large blades. Use more specific type where known. | The longest lasting industry of the Plio-Pleistocene/Early Stone Age in southern Africa and dating from about 1.3 mya to around 250 kya. It is marked by the presence of bifacial implements predominantly handaxes and cleavers that are made on a variety of stone materials. A continuation of simple tool forms including cores and flakes from the Oldowan is evidenced however retouched flakes become more common. Earliest and most securely dated evidence for this industry derives from Ethiopia."}

{"id": "7b658948-1f7e-40f4-9c19-841bc68c5360", "value": "Definition 1: A period occuring just after 2000 years ago (ca. 200-1840 CE) in southern Africa during which time communities combined cereal agriculture with livestock-keeping as well as the working of ceramics and metallurgy. The timing of each of these materials and associated practices may differ but broadly speaking they appear within the early part of the first millennium AD in southern Africa. Early farming community sites also referred to as the Early Iron Age occur predominantly on the eastern side of southern Africa which has a marked summer rainfall pattern paticularly between the latitudes 26\u00b0 and 33.5\u00b0 south. The Early Iron Age preferably termed Early Farming Communities in the southern African context is dated between 200 CE and 900 CE. This is followed by the Late Iron Age with the preferred term Late Farming Communities dating around 1000 CE and into the historic period. Absolute dates associated with cultural material markers have been linked to the spread of spread of Bantu-languages with a origins south of the Great Lakes region in East Africa. Use more specific type where known. Definition 2: A technological term which has generally been used to describe a culture system characterized not only by the use of iron for various purposes but also the building of semi-permanent villages the making of similarly decorated ceramic vessels (at least before a.d. 1000) and an economic system based on agriculture and the herding of domestic animals. After about a.d. 700 a new element in the economy is seen in the form of participation in external trading networks. Use more specific type where known. This broad period overlaps in time with the Final Later Stone Age in southern Africa as well as the historic period. | A broad period in southern Africa that marks the earliest phase of the Iron Age characterised by non-stratified communities. Several streams including the Eastern Stream (Kwale Branch) of the Urwewe Tradition in East Africa the Central Stream or Nkope branch and the Western Stream (Kalundu Branch) have been proposed. The streams form broad distinctions between different ceramic assemblages and are generally associated with the emergence of the earliest farming communities. In general this period is marked by the appearance of distinctive pottery metal working livestock-keeping and the cultivation of sorghum and millet. Communities would have followed familiar habitats including regions with a relatively high rainfall (>400mm) and along predominantly open woodland savannah ecotones preferably fertile river valley bottoms and littoral patchy forested corridors. Dated CE 200 - CE 900. Use more specific type where known. | Bambata B pottery is characterised as thick-walled eathernware with fine decoration multiple bands and cross-hatching on a long rimand/or alternating blocks of stamped and incised lines on the neck. The pottery has been recovered in Zimbabwe at Great Zimbabwe and Mabveni and in Botswana at Tswapong Hills and Maunatlala as well as several other sites in South Africa. Bambata B includes several separate shapes including jars with curved necks jars with straight necks necked bowls constricted bowls and open bowls. Bambata A is suggested to belong to the Later Stone Age Herders of southern Africa and Bambata B with farming communities. The connection between Bambata wares and the larger Kalundu ceramic tradition is debated."}

{"id": "c414bc93-6ecd-4ef5-b653-25f02f0bb1aa", "value": "The opening of the Atlantic trade in the second half of the 2nd millennium had great repercussions not only for West African societies but also for the rest of the world."}

{"id": "67ca80df-ef12-4a3d-86c0-3715aa27f810", "value": "{\"id\": \"37ef2df1-18b1-4f71-9bec-45d020eda311\", \"value\": \"The Quaternary is the second major division of geologic time in the Cenozoic era following the Tertiary period. It extends from about 2.580 million years ago to the present. It is divided into Pleistocene and Holocene epochs. | It has been suggested that the effects of humans on the global environment particularly since the Industrial Revolution have resulted in marked changes to the Earth\u2019s surface and that these may be reflected in the recent stratigraphic record. The term \u2018Anthropocene\u2019 (Crutzen 2002) has been employed informally to denote the contemporary global environment that is dominated by human activity (Andersson et al. 2005; Crossland 2005; Zalasiewicz et al. 2010). Discussions are presently ongoing to determine whether the stratigraphic signature of the Anthropocene is sufficiently clearly defined as to warrant its formal definition as a new period of geological time. The date for the start of the Anthropocene is currently being debated with some proponents suggesting that it began with the start of the Industrial Revolution (1800s) whilst others with the testing of atomic bombs in 1945. Others have suggest a date of 1950 marking the beginning of the 'Great Acceleration' in human activity. Another component of the debate includes whether the Anthropocene can be seen as different or distinct from the geological epoch of the Holocene. The International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) rejected the Anthropocene as a formal unit of the geologic timescale stating that \"Despite its rejection as a formal unit of the geologic timescale the Anthropocene will nevertheless continue to be used not only by Earth and environmental scientists but also by social scientists politicians and economists as well as by the public at large\"\"}"}

{"id": "3fcb0fbc-b4bd-4a47-a709-6c2c1a4ba2fe", "value": "{\"id\": \"da1ba6f6-7eca-40bb-b36d-5de5f77cff21\", \"value\": \"Date range: ~250CE - ~1200 CE. Description: \" the proposed chronology suggests a long occupation of the MLR between the first millennium BC and second millennium AD\". | Description: \"The Early assemblage between 500 BC and AD 200 was characterized by unslipped sand-tempered roulette-impressed pottery recovered from Fati3. This variety is common to Late Stone Age/Early Iron Age sites thoughout the Sahara and Sahel. Park (2012) found this type in Tombouze phase 1 between 500-400 BC and AD 120-330. Mauny collected several examples from an unnamed site 800m east of Goundam (IFAN-SO-52-39) and Tondiarou (IFAN-MAL-55-48) presumably from basal levels. Several thick-rimmed vessels with simple roulette impressions along the inetrior lip and exterior resemble the Fa\u00efta Facies indentified in the M\u00e9ma (MacDonald et al. 2003) and the Bandiagara escarpment (Bedaux & Lange 1983).\"\"}"}

skos:Concept.skos:prefLabel: {"id": "7e3f073c-ac5c-431f-85e7-5c74d90a57f4", "value": "Societies of the 1st and 2nd millennia CE (West Africa)"}
skos:Concept.skos:scopeNote: {"id": "92ab336e-9dcc-4f8a-a82c-f88324d7a411", "value": "{\"id\": \"16981c1f-81e4-407f-92ed-c893e78bb764\", \"value\": \"The first two millennia CE in West Africa were characterized by the emergence of large-scale urban formations such as Jenne-jeno in Mali and the development of the early kingdoms and empires which West Africa is well known for historically. This period also saw the introduction and diffusion of Islam (see Insoll 2003 cited in Religion and Ritual). Use more specific type where known. | Description: \"Further to the east on the Niger River oral tradition tells us that the hegemony of the Dia (Za or Ja) dynasties was organized at Koukia beginning in the 7th century AD from a proto-Songhay people though archaeology indicates that Gao was already occupied from the 6th century AD (Insoll 1996 2003). Islamization begins in the late 8th\u2014early 9th centuries AD.\"\"}"}

{"id": "7abea180-68a0-4b0f-8b30-1eb686a1470f", "value": "The period covers the Plio-Pleistocene through to the Neolithic and includes the Early Middle and Later Stone Ages. | The period associated with the earliest evidence of human origins and cultural behaviour 3.4mya-200kya | A subsequent development from the Oldowan marked by bifacial stone artifacts called handaxes and cleavers which broadly correspond with the emergence of Homo erectus in East Africa"}

{"id": "a07fb9b8-3560-4811-afe8-cc5fef9356fc", "value": "{\"id\": \"2c663279-9de1-4c9c-bd95-53835af68df4\", \"value\": \"~500 BCE - present | \"Early Period (Phase 1) : 500 BC-100 AD\" \"Timbuktu\u2019s prehistoric phase (c . 500\u2013400 BC to c . AD 900\u20131000)\" The most common decorative technique in Period/Phase 1 is twine impression (see Figure 6.21). Over 50% of the sherds from this Phase are decorated with twine alone. About 9% of sherds from this phase have fine channeling along the lip of the rim. When Twine is present on the early sherds it is often incorporated onto the lip of the rim (see Figure 6.35) as well as the shoulder and body. Twine 6/7 is by far the most common technique in the Phase and indeed within all other phases at Tombouze. Later in Period/Phase 1 black paint is applied to the outer surface but this is a relatively uncommmon occurrence.\"\"}"}

{"id": "24bba84c-f8f3-4072-8330-dd86f583c001", "value": "In Senegal the Paleolithic covers the period from 300000 to 13000BC. It is commonly defined as the age of carved stone and its cultures are located in four main areas: Dakar and its surroundings; the Gambia River valley and the Niokolo-Koba Park; the Fal\u00e9m\u00e9 valley; and the Senegal River valley. | The Evolved Palaeolithic dating from around 27000 to 13000 BC is widespread across Senegal. Characteristic tools are points (pedunculated and foliated) bifaces blades scrapers drills denticulated and foliated bifacial armatures."}
{"id": "7e185bb6-0b21-4dc4-a54c-b0636766e4c0", "value": "Italian colonisation of Ethiopia. Outposts from the period have been studied."}

{"id": "5c52f6b2-eb88-45c6-9e64-47370445ffd7", "value": "After the disintegration of Makuria the North of Sudan was ruled by various separate small feudal principalities which over time mostly converted from Christianity to Islam. These principalities continued to exist until the Ottoman conquest in 1820 and their rulers were often called Danaqla after the important city of Dongola. Similar events also occurred in the South although beginning slightly later after the disintegration of Alodia/Alwa and ending earlier with their coalescence under the 'Abdallab and then the Funj Sultanate. 1300CE - 1820C | The various Arab tribal federations in post-Alodia central and southern Sudan were united by 'Abdallah Jamma in the late 15th century CE before soon after being conquered by the Funj people from further south in the 16th century CE. 1475CE - 1504CE"}

{"id": "b7f47108-f8e5-4969-974c-a0946bc8f58d", "value": "{\"id\": \"e2e6ebbf-58d9-4d22-8cff-e9e6e8f94d9a\", \"value\": \"Description 1 (ceramics): \"the Tichitt Tradition first appeared in the M\u00e9ma region around 1300 cal. BC. Such pottery is termed the Early Fa\u00efta Facies (ex - Ndondi Tossokel). Within a few hundred years notable changes occur in this particular ceramic trajectory becoming the Late Fa\u00efta Facies sometime between 800 and 400 cal. BC. The Late Fa\u00efta Facies brings us some important new elements: accordion pleat roulettes proto-finewares that segue into the Middle Niger Deltawares rammed earth architecture and iron metallurgy - forming a fundamental point of transition from the Tichitt Tradition to the Phase I/II ceramics of the Inland Niger Delta around 200 cal. BC.\" Description 2 (settlement): the Tichitt Tradition (c. 1900\u2013400 BC) arose an early agropastoral economy with domestic pearl millet (Munson 1976; Amblard 1996; Fuller et al. 2007) stone architecture and a hierarchical settlement landscape (Munson 1980; Holl 1985 1993). Tichitt's socioeconomic trajectory has been researched and debated for decades with Munson's work at Dhar Tichitt during the late 1960s followed by that of new researchers there and at the other escarpments (Munson 1976 Holl 1986; Vernet 1993; Ould Khattar 1995; MacDonald et al. 2009; Amblard-Pison 2006; Person et al. 2006). Chronology has however been a perennial problem partly because the deflated nature of many key sites yields only occasional \u2018cuts\u2019 or sediment traps with datable organics though chaff tempering of the majority of Tichitt ceramics facilitates direct AMS dating of pottery. | Description: c. 1600\u20131000 BCE \"Classic Tichitt represents a major socioeconomic transformation during which most of Tichitt\u2019s main population centres developed. As well as the expansion of vast settlements of conjoined clusters of stone-walled compounds across Dhars Tichitt and Walata and as far afield as Dhar Tagant this period also saw the Tichitt tradition enter the M\u00e9ma region of the middle Niger...\"\"}"}

{"id": "c2b9be72-511f-4812-b733-39e25bd47170", "value": "{\"id\": \"4ef019da-2747-429b-9772-0005a6cb4e0e\", \"value\": \"The period prior to 1916 when Darfur was ruled by various independent polities believing to have originated in the 12th Century CE (although this beginning is less clear). 1100CE - 1916CE | The first state in modern Darfur attested to by historical and oral sources. Believed to have been pagan. The earliest reference to a polity in the area are from 1154CE by al-Idrisi; O'Fahey estimates the \"Daju hegemony\" may have begun around this point in the 12th century CE. 1100CE - 1550CE\"}"}

{"id": "b4aab518-0ada-4c51-ad3b-3c1104c1d5bb", "value": "Period when farming communities started making and using iron tools. This transition happened much earlier in Western Kenya than in the Central region the former being part of a much wider cultural development within the Great Lakes region covering four countries-Kenya Uganda Tanzania an Rwanda. 2600BP-1600CE | An iron technology complex which employed decorated bricks for the furnace shaft iron implements dimple-based pottery large open air settlements rock shelter and cave settlements the knowledge and use of domestication and the practice of agriculture covering some 400 000 square kilometers in the Interlacustrine area from Kivu in the West to the eastern shores of Lake Victoria in the East from the Nile in the Chobi area of Uganda in the North to the southern shores of Lake Victoria and to Burundi in the South. Period mainly represented by pottery wares such as Urewe that were associated with farming communities.2600BP-1600CE. | Pottery with thickened rims and bevels or flutes on pots or bowls. Hatched or grooved bands on shoulder of pots or below shoulder on bowls. Occurs in S.E. Kenya and the highlands of N.E. Tanzania"}

{"id": "d04a8b57-387c-4665-b95a-3614ae1d379c", "value": "Sites dating from this period can be found all over Senegal. But the most archaeologically rich are the sites of Gor\u00e9e Diouboye Fort de S\u00e9noud\u00e9bou and Tata Almamy. A number of other sites in eastern Senegal (Toumboura Fete Sylla Pouindi and Koussa) and in the historic landscapes of the Petite c\u00f4te de l'atlantique (Little Atlantic Coast). | The material culture specific to this period is found almost everywhere in Senegal. Ceramics one of the most characteristic materials are generally poorly made. The pastes were coarse and the finishes sketchy. Pottery therefore tends towards stylistic and decorative simplicity. The edges are generally simple and the lips are often flattened. Decorations are rare."}

{"id": "45c3b146-b0fd-4888-9b54-5e0cdc39cb0b", "value": "{\"id\": \"cd21dd01-2535-4252-8a77-6ce6b5c8e8d3\", \"value\": \"Description: \"The site of Tongo Maar\u00e9 Diabal (TMD) is a habitation mound of approximately 3 to 4.5 m in elevation and 9 ha in extent. TMD was occupied from 500 CE to 1150 CE and is thus contemporary with a major expansion of urbanism in the Middle Niger as well as being situated on the periphery of the two largest known West African polities of the era: Ghana/Wagadu (c.AD 400\u20131100) and Kawkaw/Gao (c.AD 700\u20131100) \"\"}"}

{"id": "8f2c56ee-3d4e-4134-b79e-57fb4241f146", "value": "The Neolithic period extends from 6185 to 2000BC. Its sites are spread throughout Senegal. In general they are found on the slopes of the Ogolian dunes the Grande C\u00f4te Dakar and Saint Louis. There are also numerous sites on the continental plain particularly in the center of the country (the Ferlo) and in the valleys of the Senegal and Gambia rivers as well as their main tributaries. These sites are located in varied microclimates. This variability indicates different modes of adaptation including subsistence strategies that have been adapted to varied environments where specific lithic (macro or microlithic) ceramic or bone technologies flourished. | This facies eponymous with the Cap Manuel site has a chronology between 5434 and 411 BC. The material culture is essentially characterised by lithic and ceramic remains. The lithics consist of macro-tools such as strikers nuclei elongated pieces and nucleiform planes. Ceramics which are rare are tempered by quartz laterite and gravel. The decoration consists of impressions made with a threaded comb or rolled cord."}

{"id": "1635290d-0f0e-4cb1-a8d2-5d4af7b0d6ca", "value": "{\"id\": \"501781c4-4982-4619-9af5-3265ecfdde8a\", \"value\": \"Description: \"This tradition has been recovered from every site associated by (p.39) oral tradition with the historical state of Segou. Its range of rim forms is limited (only everted thickened rims and pot lids) and its range of decoration is almost entirely different from Pre-Segovian assemblages. Likewise the paste of the Segou pottery tradition though also of tempered grog is relatively coarse with the common addition of small lateritic pebbles.\" Date range: 1600 CE - 1861CE. | ~1700 CE - 1861 CE\"}"}

{"id": "47ddc884-0de1-453b-827a-1c22b5dc46eb", "value": "{\"id\": \"a23bf333-5ad9-4268-b11d-ebc6c1bbc27c\", \"value\": \"A catch-all category for all period terms described as the \"Neolithic\" in Eastern Africa. This term generally refers to the presence of domestic plants and/or animals increased sedentism and the use of polished or ground stone tools among other markers. As the term varies in what dates and markers it refers to across different regions more specific terms should be used if possible - the dates added here refer to the maximal extents. 6000BCE - 500CE.While the term Neolithic was developed in reference to West Asia North Africa and Europe and so may have less utility while referring to Africa it is still used (and does have some parallels due to connections along the Nile). | The period is associated with the later Holocene spread of pastoralism (a way of life centred around the herding and management of livestock) throughout eastern Africa changing its socio-economic and natural landscapes. | The Elmentaitan is a group of sites identified by minimally decorated mica-tempered ceramics large blade production its own lithic tool styles nearly exclusive use of green obsidian from Mt Eburru sources cremation burials and settlement in highland areas. Settlement locations commonly on savanna/forest ecotone and open sites above 1900m and large settlements above 2600m. Removal of central incisors common: ca.3300-1200BP\"}"}

{"id": "93ba4f72-35d7-46f0-bad5-8d6ef2cfa4d7", "value": "In Senegal the Iron Age coincides with the period of invention and development of metallurgical techniques between 2000 BC and 1600 AD. The period is also known for its regional diversity in the type of material culture identified. This has allowed archaeologists to divide the period according to the different site and material markers from megaliths habitat sites tumuli to shell mounds. | The habitat sites are flattened mounds with little relief (2-5 m high) and can be grouped or isolated. Their extremely variable extents extend over several hundred meters in length and width and are sometimes covered with shards of pottery the remains of metallurgical activity (slag tuy\u00e8res) and various debris. The phenomenon of habitat sites extends without interruption from Dagana to nearly 200 km south of Bakel in a vast space between the fossilized hydrographic network of the Ferlo in the south and the Senegal River valley in the north. Elsewhere these sites are also found in the Sine-Saloum and in the south towards Kolda. | Major rim classes: SO SCL2; Twine: Multiple-stick cord-wrapped stick; possible Tw6; Decorations: Plain incisions fingernail impressions; Paste characteristics: Undetermined Characteristic vessel forms: Closed ovoid jar and Open globular bowl."}

{"id": "c6e56aa7-b324-482e-b5e8-64fa73ffcfc1", "value": "{\"id\": \"de9dbd5d-ef4a-4454-8ed8-4403d9f48e9c\", \"value\": \"13\u201319th c. AD. \"These kingdoms expanded from the Niger River to the White Volta Basin. Mossi warriors exercised pressure on the Dogon of the Plain in the 15th century and controlled the territory up to today\u2019s border of Mali and Burkina Faso causing the retreat of the Dogon to the Cliff.\"\"}"}

{"id": "2ab78817-0237-44e6-abde-e92317e21772", "value": "Dated between 1100 and 950 BC this phase is only present in Diallowalli and is characterized by pottery with simple edges. They are decorated by impressions with braided twisted or folded cord. The incisions and applied decorations are aditive motifs. A bone industry is also found which links the Diallowalli site to that of Khant."}

{"id": "3f47c152-a854-41fb-a458-67223f098ad0", "value": "The Sangoan industry (referred to as Bambesi in Zimbabwe) is considered to be a transitional lithic industry between the Later Achuelean and the early Middle Stone Age deriving predominantly north of the Limpopo River basin in southern Africa. It has been described from the Kalambo Falls site of Zambia and at sites Hope Fountain Pomongwe Bambata and Gweru Kopje and other sites around Hwange National Park Zimbabwe. The industry is characterised by the low presense of prepared cores that are absent from the Later Achuelean and by the presence of rare handaxes and cleavers core-axes core-scrapers and blade cores. Sangoan Industry is roughly thought to date from around ca. 500 - 300 ka."}
{"id": "e3a23879-40de-4a74-94ea-840af0641062", "value": "This period is characterised by the use of today\u2019s contemporary pottery such as Diola."}

{"id": "d7744b2b-1172-4532-8bf0-6ef86e21fd0e", "value": "{"id": "de35da25-a314-4062-98d9-1ec92525ab71", "value": "Analyse métallurgique
 Catégorie : Technique
 Définition : L'étude des métaux. Les artefacts métalliques et les outils ou déchets de leur fabrication sont examinés afin de reconstituer les processus de fabrication, la source des matières premières et l'utilisation.
 Cela peut être fait par les différentes techniques d'analyse chimique ou par un examen métallographique au microscope.
 Dans le cas du cuivre, du bronze et d'autres métaux non ferreux, cette analyse peut donner des informations sur les alliages, la fonte, le travail à froid et le recuit,
 Dans le cas du fer et de l'acier, on peut obtenir des informations sur le forgeage, la cémentation et la trempe et le revenu."}"}

{"id": "392c0db9-adf7-4637-bc90-5c48a0da83f8", "value": "{"id": "77b3c0f0-de8b-4ae4-8819-8b1092083ad3", "value": "Metallurgical Analysis
 Category: Technique
 Definition: The study of metals. Metal artifacts and the
 tools or waste products of their manufacture are examinedto reconstruct manufacturing processes, the source of raw
 materials, and the usage. This may be done by the various
 techniques of chemical analysis, or may involve metallo-
 graphic examination under a microscope. In the case of
 copper, bronze, and other nonferrous metals, such analysis
 may yield information about alloys, casting, cold-working,
 and annealing. For iron and steel, there may be informa-
 tion about forging, carburization, quenching, and
 tempering."}"}

{"id": "bd8f4e7e-5821-4850-b4be-cfa435f8e753", "value": "Any place where a pit was dug and a fire built, sometimes identified by charcoal, baked earth, ash, discoloration, or an outline of stones or clay footing. The site of an open domestic fire might have served as kiln or oven. Hearths often appear in one layer of soil after another as an archaeologist digs down through a site, and they are an indication of a succession of camps or habitations. Charcoal from a hearth can be dated by the radiocarbon method. Baked clay in a hearth can be dated by the paleomagnetic method. Burnt earthen rims may provide oxidized material for archaeomagnetic dating. The hearth is often centrally located and has a variety of shapes and sizes."}

{"id": "5b3fe750-92ee-472d-b046-d354320ec892", "value": "Tout endroit o\u00f9 une fosse a \u00e9t\u00e9 creus\u00e9e et o\u00f9 un feu a \u00e9t\u00e9 fait, parfois identifi\u00e9 par du charbon de bois, de la terre cuite, des cendres, une d\u00e9coloration ou un contour de pierres ou de terre battue. L'emplacement d'un feu domestique ouvert peut avoir servi de four ou de fourneau. Les foyers apparaissent souvent dans une couche de sol apr\u00e8s l'autre lorsque l'arch\u00e9ologue creuse un site, et ils sont une indication d'une succession de camps ou d'habitations. Le charbon de bois d'un foyer peut \u00eatre dat\u00e9 par la m\u00e9thode du radiocarbone. L'argile cuite dans un foyer peut \u00eatre dat\u00e9e par la m\u00e9thode pal\u00e9omagn\u00e9tique. Les rebords de terre br\u00fbl\u00e9e peuvent fournir du mat\u00e9riel oxyd\u00e9 pour la datation arch\u00e9omagn\u00e9tique. L'\u00e2tre est souvent situ\u00e9 au centre et a une vari\u00e9t\u00e9 de formes et de tailles."}

{"id": "217c6887-4057-48ef-a272-c35032602028", "value": "{"id": "90607182-cfd2-4290-aff3-7bbe8bc6faf8", "value": "The process of extracting usable metal from an ore by heating to
 extreme temperatures in a hearth or furnace. Some metals may melt while
 being smelted and these can be run off or trapped in crucibles as ingots. But
 melting metals was not necessarily the aim; the main chemical reaction in
 smelting is that of reducing a metal oxide in the form of a bloom which can
 then be further worked by forging to drive off the remaining impurities.
 Archaeological remains of the smelting process include hearths and
 furnaces containing slag, tuyères, cinder, slag, and possibly ingot fragments"}"}

{"id": "cc938138-388e-434d-a3d9-6625ac1bd52d", "value": "{\"id\": \"1d08f4bf-4dbf-405b-a678-969353bf86ff\", \"value\": \"Un monument fun\u00e9raire de la pr\u00e9histoire tardive dans les \u00eeles britanniques qui comprend un monticule circulaire de terre et de roche red\u00e9pos\u00e9e, d'un diam\u00e8tre compris entre 6 et 15 m\u00e8tres de diam\u00e8tre, qui recouvre un d\u00e9p\u00f4t fun\u00e9raire central et qui est entour\u00e9 d'un foss\u00e9 de carri\u00e8re grossi\u00e8rement carr\u00e9 ou rectangulaire. La s\u00e9pulture centrale est g\u00e9n\u00e9ralement une inhumation d'adulte et est plac\u00e9e sur l'ancienne surface du sol ou dans une fosse fun\u00e9raire. Des objets fun\u00e9raires, comprenant dans certains cas des v\u00e9hicules \u00e0 roues complets ou d\u00e9mont\u00e9s, accompagnent g\u00e9n\u00e9ralement l'inhumation.\n La plupart des tumulus carr\u00e9s datent de la p\u00e9riode de La T\u00e8ne I en Grande-Bretagne, en gros des 6e et 5e si\u00e8cles avant J.-C., et se trouvent principalement dans le Humberside et l'East Riding of Yorkshire. Un nombre croissant, cependant, est reconnu dans d'autres parties de l'Angleterre. La tradition des tumulus carr\u00e9s en Angleterre a \u00e9t\u00e9 caract\u00e9ris\u00e9e comme un \u00e9l\u00e9ment cl\u00e9 de la culture d'Arras qui a pu \u00eatre introduite dans l'est de l'Angleterre par des colons venus de France.\"}"}

{"id": "a4171b54-655b-495c-9e0a-a2505b21645d", "value": "{\"id\": \"6f32022c-077f-4f93-bbda-c54f1e0d9e1f\", \"value\": \"mine [MC].\n Tout type d'excavation dans le sol dans le but d'extraire une mati\u00e8re premi\u00e8re telle que la pierre, le minerai m\u00e9tallique, le charbon ou le silex. Les mines les plus simples sont essentiellement des puits creus\u00e9s dans le sol pour trouver ou suivre des affleurements du mat\u00e9riau d\u00e9sir\u00e9 ; elles peuvent \u00eatre d\u00e9crites comme des mines \u00e0 ciel ouvert. Les lignes de puits d'extraction peu profonds qui suivent les affleurements de minerai m\u00e9tallique sont appel\u00e9es r\u00e2teaux/andaineur. Les trous plus profonds et plut\u00f4t cylindriques peuvent \u00eatre d\u00e9crits comme des mines \u00e0 puits simple. Les exemples o\u00f9 le puits est \u00e9largi au fond pour maximiser la surface disponible pour l'extraction d'une couche particuli\u00e8re de mat\u00e9riau sont connus sous le nom de puits en cloche. Les puits qui donnent acc\u00e8s \u00e0 une s\u00e9rie de galeries qui suivent des filons de mat\u00e9riaux souterrains sont connus sous le nom de mines \u00e0 puits en galerie. Les puits qui s'enfoncent horizontalement dans la pente d'une colline ou d'une falaise en suivant le mat\u00e9riau dans la pente sont appel\u00e9s adits ou drift. Les techniques d'exploitation mini\u00e8re se sont d\u00e9velopp\u00e9es r\u00e9guli\u00e8rement \u00e0 partir de l'\u00e9poque n\u00e9olithique dans la plupart des r\u00e9gions du monde, l'utilisation de l'allumage du feu et des maillots de pierre \u00e9tant le moyen le plus commun pour extraire les roches dures jusqu'\u00e0 ce que des outils en fer ou en acier durci soient disponibles \u00e0 la fin de l'\u00e9poque m\u00e9di\u00e9vale. L'utilisation de forets et d'explosifs appara\u00eet \u00e0 partir du 18e si\u00e8cle. \u00c0 l'\u00e9poque pr\u00e9historique, les roches tendres telles que le gravier ou la craie \u00e9taient extraites \u00e0 l'aide d'outils en os et en bois de cerf et de haches en pierre et en silex. L'arch\u00e9ologie des mines et de l'exploitation mini\u00e8re est souvent assez compliqu\u00e9e car, en plus des \u00e9l\u00e9ments souterrains (qui sont souvent bien pr\u00e9serv\u00e9s), il y aura des structures de surface, y compris des terrils, des zones de traitement, des \u00e9tages de travail, une s\u00e9rie d'abris et d'installations, des ouvrages de drainage, et peut-\u00eatre des aqueducs, des foss\u00e9s, des r\u00e9servoirs et d'autres ouvrages de gestion de l'eau lorsque l'\u00e9nergie hydraulique \u00e9tait utilis\u00e9e ou lorsque les mat\u00e9riaux extraits de la mine devaient \u00eatre lav\u00e9s.\"}"}

{"id": "ae1726d3-10b2-4201-afb4-b46d04fc6695", "value": "{"id": "414c73df-f39f-49af-aad2-8c757f5b5162", "value": "mine [MC].
 Any kind of excavation into the ground for the purpose of extracting
 some kind of raw material such as stone, metal ore, coal, or flint. The
 simplest mines are basically pits sunk into the ground to find or follow
 outcrops of the desired material; these can be described as open–cast mines
 . Lines of shallow extraction pits following surface outcrops of metal ore
 are known as rakes . Deeper, rather cylindrical holes may be described as
 simple shaft mines . Examples where the shaft is expanded at the bottom to
 maximize the area available for extracting a particular layer of material are
 known as bell pits . Shafts that provide access to a series of galleries that
 follow seams of material underground are known as galleried shaft mines .
 Pits that run horizontally into a hill slope or cliff following material into the
 slope are known as adits or drift mines . The techniques of mining
 developed steadily from Neolithic times onwards in most parts of the world,
 the use of fire-setting and stone mauls being the commonest way of
 extracting hard rocks until hardened iron or steel tools became available in later medieval times. The use of drills and explosives appears from the 18th century ad. In prehistoric times, soft rock such as gravel or chalk was
 excavated using bone and antler tools and stone and flint axes. The
 archaeology of mines and mining is often rather complicated because as
 well as the underground elements (which are often well preserved) there
 will be surface structures including spoil heaps, processing areas, working
 floors, a range of shelters and facilities, drainage works, and perhaps
 aqueducts, leats, reservoirs, and other water management works where
 water power was used or where material removed from the mine itself
 needed to be washed."}"}

{"id": "94ba1713-ef17-42bf-bce8-2bbfef697dba", "value": "Excr\u00e9ments humains ou animaux (f\u00e8ces) conserv\u00e9s g\u00e9n\u00e9ralement par dessiccation, fossilisation, ou dans des conditions de saturation en eau."}

{"id": "9566de5c-e615-41c4-887c-e2a453750cb3", "value": "{"id": "db689464-e379-4d62-a1b3-fa4687056080", "value": "Moat
 Category: Structure
 Definition: A deep, broad ditch, either dry or filled with
 water, that is dug and surrounds a castle, fortification, build-
 ing, or town, historically to provide it with a preliminary line
 of defense.
 KIPFER, Encyclopedic Dictionary of Archaeology, p. 874
 moat [Co].
 A deliberately constructed ditch or cutting filled with water that
 surrounds a structure or settlement. Moats are usually constructed to
 provide a measure of defence, drainage of the central area, and/or a supply
 of aquatic food resources such as fish and fowl.
 DARVILL, Oxford Concise Dictionary of Archaeology, p. 606/1096"}"}

{"id": "47ec2cc3-6686-4dd0-a4b1-1942e2756ff1", "value": "{"id": "6705b30d-ba2d-4811-aefd-e69f3edbed06", "value": "Douves
 Catégorie : Structure
 Définition : Fossé large et profond, sec ou rempli d'eau, creusé et entourant un château, une fortification, un bâtiment ou une ville, historiquement pour lui fournir une première ligne de défense.
 
 fossé [Co].
 Fossé ou coupe délibérément construit et rempli d'eau qui entoure une structure ou un établissement. Les douves sont généralement construites par mesure de défense, le drainage de la zone centrale et/ou l'approvisionnement en ressources alimentaires aquatiques telles que les poissons et les volailles."}"}

{"id": "9f4773cb-e09f-40e5-9b7b-8d28db431464", "value": "{"id": "31b2fec0-7b55-4c97-b3ea-0bbe4d8e0cd3", "value": "Stagnosols are soils with a perched water table, 
often caused by the presence of an impermeable 
barrier deep in the soil. Perched water tables lead 
to temporary water logging and the mobilisation of 
iron and/or manganese. This process gives rise to a 
characteristic colour pattern; aggregate surfaces are 
bleached and depleted of iron whereas the centres 
are enriched showing brown to orange colours. 
A common name in many national classification 
systems is pseudogley. They have been recorded in 
Côte d'Ivoire, Central African Republic and Chad."}"}

{"id": "a41adc7d-48cc-444a-9d21-1e0ed11f7d18", "value": "{\"id\": \"d44687ef-7981-4d67-9e86-dd62a48bd51d\", \"value\": \"The defining feature of a corbeille is a circular or subcircular perimeter constructed from fl at stones or slabs embedded in the ground and usually angled outwards. Di Lernia et al. (2013) have excavated 26 corbeilles on the Messak Settafet (Libyan Fezzan) and published\nradiocarbon dates from 17 of these features, demonstrating that (along with tumuli, stone platforms and stone rings) they were associated with the ritual slaughter of large animals, predominantly cattle, and the interment of their remains, during the middle to late 6th millennium BP. Some of these monuments, including corbeilles, incorporate or are associated with standing stones on which cattle have been engraved (di Lernia 2006; di Lernia and Gallinaro 2010; di Lernia et al. 2013).\"}"}

{"id": "8f78c15c-370d-456c-b74c-87518b009db2", "value": "{\"id\": \"f728fc86-f3aa-42e3-a7b1-573f1e906392\", \"value\": \"Terme appliqu\u00e9 aux collections d'objets m\u00e9talliques de l'\u00e2ge du bronze trouv\u00e9s en Europe du Nord qui semblent repr\u00e9senter les outils et la r\u00e9serve d'un m\u00e9tallurgiste. Ainsi, ils contiennent g\u00e9n\u00e9ralement des outils et des armes bris\u00e9s, d\u00e9coup\u00e9s pour \u00eatre recycl\u00e9s, des lingots, des moules et des outils pour travailler le m\u00e9tal. On suppose que ces tr\u00e9sors \u00e9taient d\u00e9pos\u00e9s ou dissimul\u00e9s par des forgerons itin\u00e9rants par s\u00e9curit\u00e9, mais pour une raison quelconque, ils n'ont jamais \u00e9t\u00e9 en mesure de les r\u00e9cup\u00e9rer. \u00c9galement connus sous le nom de \"tr\u00e9sors de fondeurs\".\"}"}

{"id": "13d8ea37-d356-4764-a20c-aaa3fd77725f", "value": "{"id": "c68ca454-0e17-46f4-9ec6-c3a9edfa7748", "value": "Term applied to collections of Bronze Age metalwork found in northern
 Europe that appear to represent the tools and stock-in-trade of a
 metalworker. Thus they typically contain broken tools and weapons cut up
 for recycling, ingots, moulds, and tools for working metal. It is speculated
 that these hoards were deposited or concealed by itinerant smiths for safety,
 but for whatever reason they were never able to recover them. Also known
 as founder's hoards."}"}

{"id": "c530042a-6226-499c-aa9a-f78231bc518f", "value": "Un temple pour le culte d'un dieu avec des images de divinit\u00e9s, et o\u00f9 les adeptes se rendent quotidiennement au culte. Le temple de culte a atteint sa forme la plus d\u00e9velopp\u00e9e dans les grands sanctuaires \u00e9rig\u00e9s au cours de plusieurs si\u00e8cles \u00e0 Th\u00e8bes, en particulier le temple de Louxor commenc\u00e9 par Amenhotep III de la dix-huiti\u00e8me dynastie."}

{"id": "35beeb14-81c3-46e7-9ce2-18281ef392ef", "value": "{"id": "01b5048a-8631-4bd8-bdb1-3922a216e3f6", "value": "A temple for worship of a god with images of deities, andwhere the followers worshipped daily. The cult temple
 achieved its most highly developed form in the great sanctuaries
 erected over many centuries at Thebes – especially the Luxor
 Temple, started by Amenhotep III of the Eighteenth Dynasty."}"}

{"id": "6201cfc3-60d2-4af7-bd06-8463ef2693ba", "value": "Techniquement, un talus ou un mur allong\u00e9 formant la limite d\u00e9fensive d'une enceinte. La plupart des remparts sont associ\u00e9s \u00e0 des foss\u00e9s ext\u00e9rieurs qui constituent un \u00e9l\u00e9ment suppl\u00e9mentaire de la structure d\u00e9fensive. La construction des remparts varie consid\u00e9rablement, allant de simples monticules de terre et de pierre (remparts de d\u00e9charge) \u00e0 des structures \u00e9labor\u00e9es comprenant des charpentes en bois (remparts en caissons et remparts \u00e0 colombages), en passant par des murs \u00e0 rev\u00eatement en pierre. Parfois, un rempart en pierre peut \u00eatre d\u00e9lib\u00e9r\u00e9ment br\u00fbl\u00e9 pour augmenter sa r\u00e9sistance et sa stabilit\u00e9 (remparts vitrifi\u00e9s). La taille de nombreux remparts pr\u00e9historiques et ult\u00e9rieurs signifie qu'ils pr\u00e9servent fr\u00e9quemment des zones substantielles d'ancienne surface de sol qui refl\u00e8tent les conditions locales de la p\u00e9riode pr\u00e9c\u00e9dant la construction du rempart."}

{"id": "0de59140-9575-45f6-bdf6-60a093dc88fc", "value": "Technically an elongated bank or wall forming the defensive boundary of an enclosure. Most ramparts are associated with external ditches that provide an extra component of the defensive structure. The construction of ramparts varies considerably from simple mounds of earth and stone (dump ramparts) to elaborate structures involving timber frameworks (box ramparts and timber-laced ramparts), and stone revetted walls. Sometimes a stone rampart may be deliberately burnt to increase its strength and stability (vitrified ramparts). The size of many prehistoric and later ramparts means that they frequently preserve substantial areas of old ground surface that reflect local conditions in the period up to the time the rampart was built."}
